text:
alex_support: FYI customer reported a sharp p99 spike after last night's deploy, tenant ID T-8842. They hit a lot of `CUDA OOM` and timeouts. sending logs below :worried:

alex_support: logs snippet: `2026-03-16T22:14:02Z ERROR serve/runtime: cuda runtime error: out of memory (alloc_bytes=134217728) stacktrace... p99 increased from 220ms -> 1.9s`

alex_support: affected route: `/v1/generate` model: `open-redwood-13b-v1` - long chat sessions (avg tokens ~2.2k)

monitoring_bot: Alert: p99 latency spike for tenant T-8842 on route /v1/generate (90th->99th percentile increase), GPU memory pressure high on gpu-03, autoscale not triggered (reserved pool). See: https://internal.metrics/p99/T-8842

jake_sre: on it. can you paste full `dmesg`/cuda logs from gpu-03 and the runtime worker logs for the time window?

alex_support: pasting short grep: `gpu-03: [ 12345.678] cuda: out of memory at mem_alloc.c:421`

alex_support: runtime logs show repeated KV cache growth for tenant T-8842: `kv_cache.size=+~1.4GB over 10m` - looks like long contexts accumulating

liz_runtime: +1. sounds like KV growth + allocator fragmentation. we've seen similar when lots of long-chat users pin huge KV caches on a small slab allocator.

noah_oncall: quick mitigation for customer: 1) enable active-fallback to smaller model (open-redwood-7b) for that tenant 2) enforce `max_context_tokens=1024` at API layer 3) route their traffic to other pool while we triage. want me to do those? :thumbsup:

alex_support: customer agreed to temporary context limit. please apply and notify.

tom_infra: we can also restart the worker process on gpu-03 to free fragmented device memory. restarting will drop in-flight caches; schedule a low-impact restart now?

jake_sre: before restart, let's capture a heapmap and `nvprof` snapshot and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())"` to see fragmentation pattern. also capture `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` output.

alex_support: done. attaching outputs (trimmed): `torch.cuda.memory_summary(): segment/allocated_bytes: reserved=8.0G allocated=5.6G active_allocations=742 free_segments_small=128 free_segments_large=12`

liz_runtime: that reserved/allocated gap + lots of small free segments = slab fragmentation. allocator isn't coalescing due to many small evicted KV entries.`

jake_sre: root cause hypothesis: tenant's long-chat workload causes KV cache growth; combined with PyTorch caching allocator leads to fragmentation -> OOM on new allocations -> requests fall back to slower CPU path or time out -> p99 spike.

maya_billing: side note: we saw sudden token usage and cost spike for that tenant last 24h. billing team flagged. keeping them limited is fine.

noah_oncall: immediate steps I recommend: `1) apply tenant-level KV eviction policy (LRU, cap at 1GB) 2) restart worker(s) on gpu-03 to defrag 3) spin up 1 extra worker in the pool (scale out) 4) enable smaller-model fallback for this tenant`

liz_runtime: also push a short-term allocator tweak: set `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128` on the worker env to reduce fragmentation from many small frees. It's low-risk and reversible.

jake_sre: agree. sequence: capture diagnostics -> set KV cap -> set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF -> restart workers -> monitor. If p99 persists, we'll throttle requests and trigger canary rollout of a new allocator patch.

alex_support: I applied tenant context cap (1024) and enabled fallback to 7b. customer confirmed lower p99 after ~6 minutes.

monitoring_bot: Alert resolved: p99 decreased to baseline for tenant T-8842 after mitigation. GPU memory pressure dropped on gpu-03.

liz_runtime: thanks. followups: 1) add a tenant warn at 75% KV cap with automated email to account rep 2) schedule a postmortem to tune default KV caps and update docs 3) consider default `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` for runtime images

tom_infra: I'll add an infra runbook entry for targeted worker restarts and safe drain procedure (how to drain connections to avoid request loss).

jake_sre: repro steps for engineering to reproduce locally (put in ticket):
```
# repro with long-context stream
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"open-redwood-13b-v1","input":"'$(python -c 'print("x "+"\n"*2000)')'","stream":false}'
```

jake_sre: run multiple concurrent streams (10-20) from same tenant to hit KV growth. Observe `torch.cuda.memory_summary()` and p99.

alex_support: created support ticket SUP-2026-8842 and informed customer of mitigations and next steps.

maya_billing: flagged for billing review; will follow-up re: overage protection.

noah_oncall: next-day plan: run allocation profiler across busy pool, evaluate default `max_split_size_mb`, and add automated eviction when per-tenant KV > threshold. assign to liz_runtime + jake_sre.

liz_runtime: assigned. I'll open a PR with env var default + docs and a small BDFL test to validate no regression.

jake_sre: closing loop: confirm the worker restarts were done at 22:30 UTC, defrag successful, p99 stable for 2h. will write up a concise RCA for postmortem. :white_check_mark:

alex_support: thanks team. I'll update the ticket and mark customer follow-up scheduled.
